items.note6: TIER-1 LEADING INDICATOR SHIPPED 2026-08-13: verified catches on named records, per week (scripts/catch-rate.mjs, `npm run catches`). Approved 8/12, unbuilt until today. WHY IT EXISTS: G-1 has no gradient. The north-star count sat at 0 for 21 days and then jumped to 1, which told us nothing on any day in between; this answers the question that count cannot -- IS THE ADOPTED SURFACE STILL ALIVE ENOUGH TO BE WORTH STEWARDING. A month of zeros is the signal to adopt a SECOND surface, not to try harder on this one. DERIVED FROM GIT HISTORY, never hand-maintained, for the same reason README's state block is generated: a figure a human retypes weekly is stale between retypes. DEFINITION: a catch is a GENERATED pin whose `expect` string changed in a commit. That is not a proxy for record movement, it IS record movement -- generated pins are rewritten wholesale by extract-pins.mjs from the mirror, so the only way one changes is that its bounds-table row moved upstream. The editorial/record distinction falls out for free and reproduces the ledger's own recorded history exactly: 50c8096 (7/28 editorial drift -- dead cross-link, missing C in LaTeX) never touched claims.json, pins byte-identical, ZERO catches even though the mirror really drifted and the alarm really fired; da17be3 (8/02, 'first pure record movement') moved exactly the three pins its note names (10c, 38a, 71a). LIVE READING AT SHIP: 8 distinct records across 3 weeks -- w/o 7/20 = 0 (two real drifts, both editorial-or-additive), w/o 7/27 = 4 (pin:3a:L, 10c:L, 38a:L, 71a:L), w/o 8/10 = 4 from 6 movements (pin:10a:L, 10a:U, 15a:U, 2a:U). TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT WHILE BUILDING IT, both fixed, both worth keeping: (1) the first version counted pin:2a:U THREE TIMES for the 8/12 burst in which upstream reworded one attribution paragraph on three pushes -- exactly the inflation CLAUDE.md's burst rule names THIS indicator as the victim of, and I built it in anyway. Headline is now DISTINCT RECORDS per week; the raw movement count stays visible in parentheses so the burst is not hidden either. (2) pin:15a:U moved on a CITATION-KEY RENAME where every bound value was byte-identical -- so a pin can move without a record moving, and that same pin was OUR OWN PR #141 landing rather than a catch at all. NOT FIXED BY DESIGN: separating those would need to parse the value out of the cell, which symbolic cells ($K_{DR}+10^{-26}$), negatives and O(.) asymptotics defeat, and would put an unverified mathematical judgment in our own ledger. THE PIN RULE APPLIES TO THE INDICATOR BUILT ON IT -- it asserts LISTING POSITION MOVED, never 'a record moved'. The figure is therefore an UPPER BOUND and says so on every run rather than in a doc nobody re-reads. KP-78 BOTH ANSWERS: selftest fires on a moved generated pin and is silent on unchanged / added (upstream adding 86a is not a catch) / removed / hand-claim edits / the commit before the file existed. Fixtures not git history, deliberately -- actions/checkout is depth-1, so a history-walking selftest would pass locally and be untestable in CI, which is the test-it-from-the-environment-that-runs-it rule. The CI-wiring guard was itself negative-controlled: deleting the new workflow step makes reverify.test.mjs exit 1 naming `node scripts/catch-rate.mjs --selftest`, restoring it exits 0 at 19 workflow steps / 13 selftests, with `git diff --numstat` proving the mutation landed first. The indicator itself never runs in CI: it renders a figure and no verdict, so there is nothing for a build to fail on -- same class as traffic-snapshot.mjs and gap-table.mjs. TIGHTENED SAME DAY after orchestrator management feedback on the P1 retro (msgId 5d328105), three changes, all shipped: (i) THE EMITTED LINE IS NOW SELF-DESCRIBING -- header reads 'Record-listing MOVEMENTS per week -- a CEILING on catches, not a count of them', because a reader who skips the caveat quotes whatever the header called it, and as built the figure asserts listing position moved and includes our own PR #141. The asymmetry that makes this safe is worth stating: THE POSITIVE SIDE IS AN ACTIVITY CEILING, THE ZERO SIDE IS EXACT -- a zero on an upper bound is a true zero -- and the decision rule attached to it ('a month of zeros means adopt a second surface') consumes only the zero side. (ii) THE PER-WEEK-QUOTE CONVENTION IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, in CLAUDE.md and in the script's own output: quote the PER-WEEK figure, never the running total, which answers no question we ask of it and only ever grows, so it reads as progress by construction. This closes the gap the retro itself named as 'not written down anywhere'. (iii) DEDUCTION TRIGGER RECORDED, deliberately not built: deduct our own merged PRs from the positive figure BEFORE ANY POSITIVE FIGURE GOES OUTWARD, or once own-PR pins exceed roughly one a month. At N=1 (pin:15a:U, PR #141) the deduction is not worth building, and git cannot see whose commit upstream merged, so the mechanism would be a list of our own merged PR shas kept here. STANDING PATTERN NAMED BY THE SAME FEEDBACK, worth more than this item: WHEN A RULE NAMES A SPECIFIC CORRUPTION, ADOPTION MEANS A TEST THAT ASSERTS IT, not a resolution to re-read the rule. The burst-inflation rule was prose on 8/12 and I built the inflation in anyway on 8/13; it is a mechanism now.
items.note7: TIER-1 INDICATOR DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-15, in the instrument shipped two days earlier. FOUND BY READING ITS OWN PRINTED OUTPUT during the steward cadence, not by a check: `npm run catches` showed THREE week rows for a FOUR-week repo. catch-rate.mjs built its week buckets from `git log -- ledger/claims.json`, so a week in which nothing committed that file was ABSENT rather than ZERO -- the week of 2026-08-03 simply did not exist in the table (git log confirms no commit touched the file between da17be3 on 2 Aug and 7018cce on 11 Aug, so that week was genuinely dry). THE COSMETIC HALF IS ONE MISSING ROW; THE LOAD-BEARING HALF IS THE COUNTER. The trailing dry-week count walked those same buckets, so it could only count weeks that were PRESENT -- and in a real drought NOTHING commits claims.json, because that file is rewritten only by extract-pins.mjs after a --snapshot and a snapshot happens only on drift. The quiet weeks never entered the map, the backward walk hit the last ACTIVE week immediately, and the count stopped at 1. The rule this indicator carries is 'a month of zeros is the signal to adopt a SECOND surface'. A month is four. THE COUNTER COULD NOT REACH TWO. This is the lane's founding defect for the third time -- an alarm that could not fire (7/24), a checker that read a sign-in page as a stale brief (8/02), and now a counter whose maximum sat below its own threshold; all three printed something that looked informative. BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED (KP-78): pre-fix, executed against one active week plus four calendar weeks of silence, 'weeks printed: 2026-07-06 2026-08-03 / dryWeeks reported: 1 / actual quiet weeks: 4'; post-fix the same shape asserts five keys plus the current week with trailingDry 4, with the negative controls asserted beside it (an unbroken run gains no rows; a movement in the newest week reads 0 dry). CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW LANE, first use in this lane and it paid for itself: catch-rate.mjs is a TRUSTED-PRINT INSTRUMENT (a script whose printed line a later reader believes) and also composes stored state across time, so the branch was held from main and the review requested (bus f2cbd000) before merging. Verdict SURVIVES with one pre-merge fix and two P2 edges, all three applied. F1, MATERIAL AND THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE THING TODAY: fillDryWeeks fills up to AND INCLUDING the current week and my trailingDry counted it, so on the Monday a drought completed its THIRD week the counter would read 4 and fire the adopt rule up to six days early. The printed table labels that row '(current, partial)' -- but THE LABEL SITS ON THE SURFACE A HUMAN READS WHILE THE RULE ACTS ON THE NUMBER. I had just shipped a fix whose entire argument was that the caveat was on the wrong surface, and put the next caveat on the wrong surface in the same file. A reviewer who had never seen the decision rule caught it; a self-review of my own rule did not. Fixed: trailingDry now takes the current week and skips it, and skips anything dated after it, so the rule needs four COMPLETED weeks; a movement still breaks the streak wherever it lands, because if the surface moved this week it is not dry whatever the completed-week count would say. F2: commit weeks came from git's %as, the author-LOCAL date, while 'today' came from a UTC clock, so a Sunday-evening commit in a negative-offset zone could read as an immediate dry week -- both sides now use the local calendar date. F3: a future-dated key from author clock skew sat beyond the fill target with a gap in front of it -- the fill now runs to whichever of the current week and the last key is later, and out-of-range weeks are EXCLUDED FROM THE COUNT rather than dropped from the table, because a phantom row is a display problem and silently discarding data would be worse. Commits c64fcd9 (fix) + 1179961 (review findings), merged --no-ff as 8ca908a so c64fcd9 keeps the sha the daily report cites; 13/13 self-tests and CI green on the merge commit. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-15-the-dry-week-counter-could-not-count-a-drought.md. STANDING CONSEQUENCE: request the review lane for the next in-class diff without being asked -- one posted line and about forty minutes of waiting returned a boundary error in the exact figure a decision rule consumes.

Orchestrator-approved with conditions in the P1 management feedback of 2026-08-17T15:47:00.896Z, which also flags the 8/22 close question upward to David. Previous wording preserved verbatim in closeWhenPrevious.  WHY: leg (a) previously read "30-day green CI". THAT IS NOT WHAT HAS BEEN COUNTED, and the gap was never a mistake -- it was the operating rule, undocumented. The 2026-08-14 scheduled run FAILED on genuine upstream drift (upstream added Martinet constant, resolved in 433091b) and the streak was deliberately NOT reset, because this lane rules that a red drift run is the alarm working. On 2026-08-17 four more reds were filed on transport failures (HTTP 429/502 reaching the mirror sources) and likewise do not reset it. A literal reading of the old wording would have reset the streak twice and G-1 could effectively never close while the project was SUCCEEDING at its purpose. The reword documents the rule; it does not move the bar. That distinction is the whole reason this was surfaced rather than edited quietly five days before the leg fires.  WHAT COUNTS AS ARMED AND FUNCTIONING: the alarm carried information every day -- it could have gone red and did go red exactly when its inputs moved. A red does NOT reset the streak when its cause is (i) a record actually moving, or (ii) a cited source being unreachable, because unreachable means unverified and reporting green there would launder an unverifiable result into a pass. A red DOES reset the streak when the cause is OUR OWN INSTRUMENT failing -- a broken checker, or worse, a GREEN THAT COULD NOT HAVE GONE RED. That second case is why day 1 is 2026-07-24 and not the 2026-07-23 CI ship date: the 7/23-7/24 greens were green-by-construction because piped steps masked exit codes, so they carried no information and the clock was restarted (see note2).  DAY 1 = 2026-07-24. DAY 30 = 2026-08-22. As of 2026-08-17 the streak is day 25 and leg (b) has been satisfied since the 2026-08-11 merge of teorth/optimizationproblems#141, so BOTH legs are on course to be met on 2026-08-22. Closing G-1 remains a surfaced decision, not a self-approval.

items.streakDayRule: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-17, BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS KNOWN, and deliberately in the direction that costs us.  THE HOLE THIS CLOSES, which I created earlier today: the reworded leg (a) says a red does not RESET the streak when its cause is an unreachable source. It did NOT say whether such a day COUNTS toward the 30. That omission was invisible until GitHub went into a critical outage (opened 2026-08-17T13:40:03Z, still unresolved at 16:36Z) five days before the leg completes, which makes it likely rather than hypothetical that one of runs 26-30 cannot fetch its sources. Deciding this on 2026-08-22, with a goal on the line and an obvious incentive to count generously, is exactly the decision nobody should be making under pressure.  THE RULE. A day counts toward the 30 if and only if that day's SCHEDULED run REACHED A VERDICT -- it completed and either confirmed no drift, or detected drift. Both are the alarm answering the question. A day whose scheduled run COULD NOT REACH A VERDICT -- it failed to fetch the cited sources, so nothing was actually verified -- does NOT count toward the 30, and does NOT reset it either. It PAUSES the clock, pushing the completion date out by one day per such day.  WHY PAUSE RATHER THAN COUNT OR RESET. Armed and functioning means the alarm ANSWERED the question. A run that could not fetch did not answer it, so counting it would inflate the streak with days that verified nothing -- the same laundering of an unverifiable into a pass that this repo refuses everywhere else (manual:true claims report UNVERIFIED, the brief check reports UNVERIFIABLE, the shallow-clone catch count reports UNKNOWN). Resetting would be equally wrong: nothing about our instrument failed, and a reset would punish us for someone else's outage and make the leg effectively unreachable during any multi-day infrastructure incident. Pause is the only reading that is honest in both directions, and it is the one that delays our own goal, which is why it is being written down now instead of on 08-22.  MECHANICAL TEST for could-not-reach-a-verdict, so this is not a judgment call later: the run's log carries an `error: fetch` line or UNREACHABLE claim lines, AND zero BROKEN claim lines, AND zero CHANGED/ADDED/ REMOVED mirror verdicts. That is precisely the signature of all six failures on 2026-08-17. A run with any BROKEN line or any mirror verdict DID reach a verdict and counts.  STATUS AS OF 2026-08-17: 25 of 25 days counted -- every scheduled run 07-24..08-17 reached a verdict (23 no-drift, 2 drift-detected), and all of them fired around 09:2x UTC, before today's outage window. Day 30 is 2026-08-22 IF runs 26-30 all reach verdicts. Each that does not moves the date out by one day.  NOT YET MECHANISED: a script that classifies each scheduled run against the test above and prints the streak day. It is a trusted-print instrument feeding a goal-close decision, so it routes through the cross-family review lane rather than being written on impulse -- and two of this lane's diffs are already queued there. Until it exists the classification is done by reading run logs, which is what produced the figures above. The RULE not existing was the risk; the script is a convenience.

If the GitHub outage is still open, record the affected days UNKNOWN and say so rather than counting them.

items.title: Alarm files NO finding issue when the job fails before the drift/claims steps run (self-test failure path)
items.note: Found by the 2026-07-25 gate-execution sweep by EXECUTING reverify.yml's `Open finding` body under GitHub's exact shell semantics (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`), not by reading it. When either self-test step fails, `finding.txt` is never created; the step's `cat finding.txt` then exits 1 under `-eo pipefail`, so the step dies BEFORE `gh issue create` and no finding issue is filed. Two consequences: (1) an instrument failure produces a red job but no issue — the drift alarm is silent about its own breakage, which is the same family as the 2026-07-24 never-armed defect; (2) the only diagnostic emitted is `cat: finding.txt: No such file or directory`, which points at the wrong thing. NOT a drift-masking bug: the job still goes red and the workflow-failure notification still fires, so a real drift is never hidden. Severity LOW. Evidence: with finding.txt absent the step exits 1; with a real synthetic drift present it produces title `Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)`, and with a real BROKEN claim it produces `Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)` — both branches of the title extractor verified FIRING against real tool output.
items.closeWhen: The Open-finding step either files a legibly-titled instrument-failure issue when finding.txt is absent, or a deliberate decision is recorded that a red job alone is sufficient for self-test failures.
items.resolution: FIXED 2026-07-25, same day, David-decided. He chose filing an instrument-failure issue over treating a red job as sufficient — rationale: a red CI run on a once-a-day lane is easy to scroll past, and the failure mode being hidden is our own instrument going quiet, which is precisely what this lane claims to catch. The Open-finding step now branches on `[ -s finding.txt ]`: with check output it behaves exactly as before ('Drift: <what moved>'); without it, it files 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (<date>)' with an explicit '(no check output — the job failed before the drift/claims steps ran)' body instead of dying at `cat` and filing nothing. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: the step body was extracted verbatim from the deployed YAML, the `gh issue create` call stripped, and run under GitHub's exact shell (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`) against all three real inputs — absent finding.txt => 'Instrument failure: bounds-ledger self-test (2026-07-25)'; real injected mirror drift => 'Drift: constants/21a.md (2026-07-25)'; real broken pin => 'Drift: claims pin:10a:U (2026-07-25)'. No regression on the two paths that already worked; pipefail guard still passes (step keeps `shell: bash`).

ORIGINAL: READY FIX (deliberately NOT shipped in the sweep — it changes WHEN the alarm files, and the alarm surface is this lane's most load-bearing artifact; 7/24's lesson is that changes here get deliberated): guard the cat and make the title honest, e.g. `cat finding.txt 2>/dev/null || echo '(no check output — job failed before the drift/claims steps ran; see the failed step above)'` plus a title fallback that says instrument-failure rather than `Drift:`. Decide first whether a self-test failure SHOULD file an issue at all — arguably yes, since a steward whose instrument breaks silently is the exact failure mode this lane exists to prevent.

Cost model: a false 'Drift:' burns a reader's time hunting a record change that never happened, and repeated flakes train us to skim past Drift: issues, which is how a REAL drift gets missed. Finding: docs/findings/2026-07-25-alarm-called-a-network-flake-a-drift.md.

items.note4: RECURRED AND RE-FIXED 2026-08-17, and the recurrence says this item was CLOSED ON A PARTIAL FIX. A-5 closeWhen reads "a tool/network error produces an honestly-titled issue that states the cause". That was true of the path A-5 actually examined -- an ^error: line in finding.txt -- and false of the other path into the same failure. check-claims.mjs reports a source it could not fetch as UNREACHABLE, and the title extractor grouped UNREACHABLE with BROKEN. Those are different events: BROKEN means the cited source WAS read and the pinned string was gone (a record moved); UNREACHABLE means it was never read. Because UNREACHABLE populated , it matched BEFORE the elif that tests for ^error:, so the A-5 fix was unreachable code for this input class -- reverify own "error: fetch constants/11a.md: 429" sat in the same finding.txt, unread.  FOUND IN PRODUCTION, not by a check, and while doing something else: dispatching reverify.yml on the held guard branch (workflow_dispatch is the ONLY route -- the workflow declares push: branches:[main], so a feature branch gets zero runs from pushing). The job hit HTTP 429 from raw.githubusercontent.com and filed issue #15 titled "Drift: claims C-1,pin:12a:U pin:37a:U,pin:37a:L pin:3c:U,pin:3c:L" -- asserting six records moved. A local npm run check four minutes earlier read 113 files in sync and 231 of 233 claims holding, so zero had. A second dispatch filed #17 naming ~30 pins.  SECOND, LATENT DEFECT IN THE SAME LINE: paste -sd", " does not join with ", ". -d takes a LIST of delimiters applied CYCLICALLY, so 3+ items came out "a,b c,d". Visible in #15 own title, and latent in every multi-file drift title before it (2 items consume only the first delimiter, which is why nobody saw it). Fixed with paste -sd, - | sed s/,/, /g.  FIX: precedence is now mirror movement (CHANGED/ADDED/REMOVED) -> claim movement (BROKEN) -> unreachable sources -> tool error -> generic, and UNREACHABLE gets its own title, "Check error: bounds-ledger could not reach N cited source(s)". GUARDED in reverify.test.mjs, which EXTRACTS the step body from the deployed YAML rather than restating it -- a copy would test the transcription and not the alarm, which is A-4 method. Seven cases under GitHub exact shell, including that a real move OUTRANKS a concurrent flake (a 429 must never mask a genuine drift). Negative control: restoring UNREACHABLE to the drift group fails the test, mutation proven to land first (git diff --numstat 20 2).  THE GUARD FOOLED ITSELF FIRST AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING: its first version resolved bash from PATH, which this machine PowerShell does not have. The spawn failed, the harness returned an empty string, and assert.doesNotMatch(title, /^Drift:/) PASSED ON THE EMPTY STRING -- a guard reporting success because it had not run. KP-78 is usually read as "prove it fires"; this is the other half, prove that a non-firing result means the CONDITION is absent rather than the INSTRUMENT. It now asserts a title was emitted at all, resolves bash via git --exec-path, and prints SKIPPED naming what went unchecked if it cannot -- the same refusal to launder an unanswerable question into a pass that the manual:true claims (UNVERIFIED), the brief check (UNVERIFIABLE) and the shallow-clone catch count (UNKNOWN) already make.  THE RED WAS CORRECT AND STAYS CORRECT. An unreachable source means we could not verify; a green there would launder an unverifiable into a pass. Only the title was wrong and only the title changed. Do NOT make 429 non-fatal. Whether the fetch layer should RETRY on 429 is a separate and real question -- that extends reach rather than softening a verdict -- and it touches two trusted instruments network paths, so it belongs behind the cross-family review lane.  CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (this note first asserted SELF-INFLICTED CAUSE, recorded: I caused the rate limit -- THAT WAS WRONG and is retracted). Two dispatches in ten minutes, ~220 fetches each, on top of the daily scheduled run. Dispatching this workflow spends a shared budget the SCHEDULED run depends on, and the first run had already answered the question. Also: a throwaway debug one-liner escaping failed to strip gh issue create before executing the step body and filed a real issue (#16) against the public repo, closed within minutes; the in-repo harness asserts the strip succeeded before running anything, the debug script did not.  HOUSEKEEPING DONE THE SAME DAY: seven issues closed, open count now 0 (verified via REST after the GraphQL listing returned 503 -- a failed query is not evidence of absence). Five of them (#10-#14) were RESOLVED drifts from 11/12/14 August that nobody closed at resolution time, each closed naming its resolving commit (d30d4e4, ec01082, 4d06395, 433091b). Five standing Drift: issues on a repo whose pitch is noticing stale things teaches the next reader that Drift: issues can be ignored, which is the precondition for missing a real one. CLOSING ON RESOLUTION IS PART OF THE DRIFT CYCLE, not optional tidying.  STATUS: fix committed on branch alarm-title-honesty (4153c00), NOT merged -- held for the cross-family review lane, because the alarm issue title is the most-read line this repo produces and is squarely in the trusted-print class. Merge it BEFORE guard-catch-count-v2 so main alarm is honest before any push-triggered run can mis-title a flake. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-17-the-alarm-called-a-rate-limit-a-record-movement.md
items.note5: ATTRIBUTION RETRACTION 2026-08-17, filed the same day and worth more than the fix it corrects. note4 above, the finding, the commit message, CLAUDE.md gotcha and two issue-closing comments all stated flatly that I CAUSED the rate limit by dispatching reverify.yml twice in ten minutes. THAT ATTRIBUTION IS RETRACTED. GitHub was in a CRITICAL OUTAGE from 2026-08-17T13:40:03.629Z -- verified by reading githubstatus.com/api/v2/incidents/unresolved.json directly rather than inheriting the orchestrator broadcast; impact critical, Actions degraded from 13:42Z, roughly 20% error rates across API / Issues / PRs / Actions. MY FIRST DISPATCH WAS 14:32Z, FIFTY-TWO MINUTES AFTER THE OUTAGE BEGAN, and Actions was already degraded before it.  THREE PIECES OF DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE WERE IN HAND AT THE TIME AND WERE NOT ASSEMBLED: (1) a LOCAL npm run check issuing ~450 raw fetches ran FULLY GREEN at 14:28Z -- 48 minutes into the outage and four minutes before the first dispatch, so volume was plainly not yet the problem; (2) a LATER local check 429d, and my dispatches were RUNNER-side, sharing no egress with this machine, so they cannot explain a residential-IP failure; (3) the errors included 502 AND 503, which no volume of requests produces. I actually WROTE "the 502 is not explainable that way" in a bus note and left the self-blame standing everywhere else.  WHAT SURVIVES: two dispatches in ten minutes is still poor practice -- each run is ~450 requests -- and the do-not-dispatch-repeatedly guidance stands. It stands as PRACTICE, not as the diagnosis of this incident. b1 (pull_request trigger, shipped today) removes most of the reason to dispatch at all.  WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE TITLE FIX IT SITS BESIDE: this lane exists to catch confident causal stories attached to record movements that were never verified. I published one about my own infrastructure, in the same document where I fixed the alarm for doing the equivalent. SELF-BLAME FELT LIKE RIGOUR AND WAS JUST ANOTHER UNVERIFIED ATTRIBUTION -- and it is the more seductive kind, because nobody challenges you for blaming yourself. The repo already had the governing rule: a POSITIVE CONTROL before any absence or cause claim. Apply it to causes you find flattering to admit.  CI CONSEQUENCE, per the fleet incident guidance: every CI conclusion in the 13:40Z-onward window is UNKNOWN, never red and never green. The two PR runs that completed success at 16:11Z did execute every step including the network legs -- positive evidence, and a positive match is self-validating -- but they are recorded UNKNOWN-with-timestamp rather than green, because a conclusion drawn from a majorly-degraded Actions service is not one this repo should lean on. Note the RED-vs-CODE distinction still holds separately: the run correctly reported it could not verify, which is our alarm working, and is not a verdict about our code either way.

items.onTrigger:
When you are about to ship anything whose job is to DETECT (test, guard, lint, probe, --check mode, alarm), before committing: (1) construct the condition it exists to catch and confirm it FIRES, naming what it printed; (2) restore and confirm it goes SILENT; (3) prove the mutation actually landed with git diff --numstat BEFORE believing either result -- a control written with 
 against these CRLF files silently no-ops and manufactures a false inert verdict (2026-07-25); (4) paste both outputs into the commit message or finding doc. If nothing in the repo currently trips it, build a fixture that does -- a detector validated only against a clean world tells you nothing. Then ask the second question, which is NOT the same: can it see the SHAPE of failure that matters, or only one direction of it? (2026-07-31: both detectors passed can-it-fire and both were blind to a class this lane exists to catch.) Finally: is it wired into something that RUNS on its own? A check only in npm scripts is not a detector.

Its selftest additionally proves it fires on a stale COUNT (not just a sha), raises on missing markers, and that its own mutations land. items.note: Found during the 2026-08-14 drift cycle, in the constant upstream added that same morning (e70b4a4, an upstream sha; it does not exist in this repo). constants/87a.md's record row says rd <= 3^4*5^4*7^4*13^2*29^4*53^2*109^2 <= 857.5662. That product is 484887097019201067725625, a 24-digit integer, so the inequality as typeset is false and the root notation is missing. Supplying the 8th root the sentence itself invites (an 8-th root class-field tower, 2-class group of rank 8) gives 913.492694, which to six significant figures is 913.493 -- the value on the [Mar2006] row directly above it. No integer degree yields 857.5662 (the required degree is 8.0748), and single-factor transcription slips do not explain the gap (the needed product is 2.926e23 against the stated 4.849e23, a ratio of 1.657, which is not a prime power). WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the row is internally inconsistent, by exact integer arithmetic on the page's own text, with the factorization re-extracted mechanically from the mirror rather than re-typed. WHAT IS NOT: what [HMR2019] actually proves. arXiv:1901.04354 is the right paper (positive control: its abstract independently names the refined Golod-Shafarevich criterion, the mechanism the row cites) but states no numeric value, the same wall three abstracts put up on 2026-07-24. So the defect is in the WITNESS, not necessarily in the bound, and two readings survive: the factorization belongs to the [Mar2006] row, or it is the right construction with a different error. items.noteInstrument: SAMPLER STOOD UP 2026-08-09, which is what this watch's onTrigger asked for and nobody had built: the traffic API retains 14 days, so the 90-day visitor count cannot be reconstructed later — it has to be accumulated. `scripts/traffic-snapshot.mjs` (npm run traffic) merges the daily views/clones window into continuity/traffic.json and prints days-since-flip plus the running totals. It renders NO verdict; the fair-read judgment stays with whoever adjudicates this watch, same reason a generated pin asserts listing position and never 'the record'. Auth is delegated to the `gh` CLI, so no traffic credential enters this now-public repo and the sampler deliberately does NOT run in CI; only its merge is guarded there (10th self-test), because a merge that returned just the incoming window would silently destroy every day older than 14 — the one bug that would eat the record we are building. Both sides demonstrated at write time per W-4/KP-78: with the truncating merge in place the self-test exits 1 naming the dropped history, with it restored exit 0. FIRST SAMPLE (taken 2026-08-09; a dated historical anchor, NOT a current reading — for the live figure run npm run traffic, which derives it from continuity/traffic.json), and it needs reading carefully rather than celebrating: 14 days recorded, 1 unique viewer-day since the flip, 25 unique cloner-days. THE CLONE FIGURE IS NOT ARRIVALS — 74 clones / 25 uniques all landed on 8/08, the day we ourselves cloned the remote repeatedly to verify the history rewrite, plus CI checkouts and whatever crawls a repo the minute it goes public. Views are the honest metric and they read 1. MEASUREMENT LIMIT FOUND, and it changes how this watch must be read: GitHub dedupes uniques only WITHIN a 14-day window, so a 90-day figure can only be a SUM of per-day uniques, which counts a returning visitor once per day. That sum is an UPPER BOUND on distinct people — which is the useful direction here: a sum under 100 conclusively settles that the threshold is NOT met, while a sum over 100 does not settle that it is. The closeWhen's '100 unique visitors' is therefore not directly measurable and must be read as 'upper bound at least 100, then look harder'.
items.note2: WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT / make me revert or replace it: an issue arriving that is NOT about the ledger's correctness (support questions, feature requests, spam) at a rate that makes the channel noise rather than signal; or a real correction arriving by some OTHER route (a PR, an upstream comment, an email) while the issue tracker stays empty — which would say the invitation is in the wrong place, not that nobody wanted to speak. items.title: MIRROR BLIND CLASS: README.md is not mirrored, and it is where upstream states which records it stands behind
items.note: Found inside the 2026-08-02 fourth-drift cycle (A-2 note6). We mirror constants/** + manifest.json (111 files); upstream README.md is NOT in the mirror. Commit dee1660 -- 'Mark C_21 and C_71 unverified records with asterisks in README' -- restored the peer-reviewed OT2013 value as the headline anchor for C_71 and marked the Numaro n=18 record (merged minutes earlier, PR #130) as unverified because it is on Zenodo but not yet peer-reviewed. Our drift alarm reported three constants files and was SILENT on the semantically largest change of the day. WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING, not academic: generated pins assert listing position inside the per-constant tables, while README is where upstream declares which of those rows it will STAND BEHIND. A record demoted from headline to asterisked is a real event -- arguably the most decision-relevant kind for anyone citing these numbers -- and we cannot see it. Same shape as BC-2 (A-11): the instrument is blind to the class the lane most exists to catch. SEPARATE FROM A-11, which is about check-claims' presence-test on OFF-mirror sources; this one is about the SCOPE of the mirror itself.
items.closeWhen: Either UPSTREAM's README.md (teorth/optimizationproblems' generated 421KB index — NOT this repo's own README.md) joins the mirrored surface with the drift alarm demonstrated firing on an asterisk/headline change and silent on an unrelated edit (W-4), OR a deliberate decision is recorded that the verified/unverified distinction is out of scope for this ledger, with the reason.
items.onTrigger: Before adopting: check how often README churns. It is a GENERATED table (the 8/01 research noted it is the repo's rendered index, 421KB), so a whole-file byte mirror may be as permanently-red as teorth/erdosproblems' problems.yaml was -- which is exactly why A-6 chose entry-level pins over a mirror there. The likely right shape is the A-6 shape: pin the specific README cells for constants we already track, not the file. Decide that before writing code.

verifyBy.method: demonstrate both sides per W-4 -- an asterisk/headline change on a tracked constant must fire, an unrelated README edit must not

items.resolution: CLOSED 2026-08-10 by the first branch of its own closeWhen: upstream README.md joined the mirrored surface, with the drift alarm demonstrated BOTH ways. Greenlit off the capacity ask (David's fire-don't-wait blanket) as the lane's #1 candidate. WHAT SHIPPED: file maps are now keyed by REPO-RELATIVE path (constants/1a.md, README.md) instead of bare filename, so a report names files as upstream does -- the old code prefixed 'constants/' by concatenation and would have printed 'constants/README.md', a lie about where the file lives inside an artifact whose whole value is being literally true. Nothing moved on disk: the 111 constants files stayed put, README sits beside them at the mirror root, and git diff --numstat after the re-snapshot showed ZERO content lines changed in any constants file (manifest + two scripts + one new file). Post-snapshot ratchet ran: extract-pins regenerated BYTE-IDENTICAL (220 generated + 9 hand), independently confirming no bounds-table row moved. Mirror 111 -> 112 files @ dee1660; ledger unchanged at 229 claims / 227 hold / 0 broken / 2 unverified. BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED, wired into reverify.test.mjs so it is guarded on every CI run: FIRES -- append an asterisk to a real README table row in upstream's own convention, check exits 1 reporting CHANGED README.md with the row verbatim; SILENT (restored) -- put it back and the same run exits 0; SILENT (unrelated edit) -- tamper a constants file and the verdict list is EXACTLY 'CHANGED constants/<file>', README not dragged in (without this, a mirror reporting every file on every run would pass the FIRES assertion while carrying no information); REMOVED -- delete the mirrored README and it reports REMOVED rather than passing silently. NEGATIVE CONTROL PERFORMED with the mutation proven to land first (files are CRLF): ROOT_FILES=[] gives 'AssertionError: an asterisked README row should exit 1, got 0' -- the alarm goes silent on exactly the event class it was built for; restoring returns PASS. THE ITEM OVERSTATED ITS OWN COST BY ~17x AND THAT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: closeWhen described a 'generated 421KB index'; the file is 24KB. The 421KB figure belongs to a DIFFERENT repo's README (teorth/erdosproblems, from A-6 scoping) and was copied across at write time. That wrong number is a plausible reason the item sat eight days -- 421KB of near-daily churn reads like a permanently-red alarm waiting to happen, which this lane refuses to ship; 24KB of curated table does not. The estimate, not the value, kept it parked. The check that would have caught it costs one curl: an item's description of its own cost is a claim like any other, and this repo does not accept unexecuted claims from anyone, including itself. ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG FIRST TIME AND THE ALARM WAS RIGHT: the unrelated-edit check originally asserted the string 'README.md' was absent from the report and failed immediately, because the report HEADER names the whole watched surface. Body was correct throughout. Fixed by asserting on verdict lines rather than raw text, which is also stricter -- it now pins the exact SET of files named. SCOPE HONESTY: this watches upstream's DECLARATION about its records, not the mathematics; a byte-mirror fires on any README edit including a typo fix, accepted deliberately because the file is small and the alternative (pinning only table spans) would reintroduce a blind class to avoid a minor annoyance. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-w5-the-readme-is-where-upstream-says-what-it-stands-behind.md.

items.note: DAVID'S RULING, 2026-08-06, in-session after reading OpenAI's Ten Advances paper: that this was the kind of work he wanted this lane doing — then, on the four-step plan (gap table → pick 2-3 under-studied targets → LLM-proposes / local-verifier-scores search loop → exact reverify + literature check + adversarial review + David-gated PR): to do all four steps. SCOPE HONESTY, recorded at write time: we play the CONSTRUCTION game (an explicit object plus a finite certificate a script can check), never the theorem game (asymptotic proofs need mathematicians or Lean, which we do not have). The certificate IS the contribution — a claim ships only with a verifier the maintainer can run. GUARD: the late-2025 'solved 10 Erdos problems' embarrassment (a model rediscovering known results) is the named failure mode; the literature/priority check is a mandatory step, not hygiene. STEP 1 DONE same day: scripts/gap-table.mjs (selftest wired into npm test + CI) — 111 constants, 65 with a numeric gap, 6 parse-suspect (instrument flags, listed in docs/gap-table.json), 40 symbolic. items.note3: ROUND ONE RAN 2026-08-07: 11 proposed constructions, 0 certified, 11 eliminated (edge-bound 5, k9-free 2, chromatic 4). Instrument: search/27b/propose-round.mjs, 8th self-test, wired into npm test + CI and proven both ways (each of 4 gates fires and stays silent; split search returns both outcomes; Sulanke re-certifies at target 9; and the CI wiring itself was negative-controlled — removing the workflow step made reverify.test exit 1 naming the unguarded selftest, restoring it returned exit 0 / 8 self-tests). FINDING (docs/findings/2026-08-07-g2-27b-round-one-the-one-edge-vise.md): two unrelated families land EXACTLY one short. The join family successor C5+K7 is over the 6n-12 budget by exactly ONE edge and has omega=9; buying that edge back from inside the clique meets budget exactly and drops omega to 8 but gives chi=9, buying it back from the join keeps omega=9 and dies on the clique gate. Independently, circulants sized to fit the budget top out at C17(1..5) with chi=9. Both directions arrive at nine. The vise: thickness 2 caps average degree below 12 so a 10-chromatic biplanar graph sits near the Brooks boundary where structure is pushed toward near-complete, while thickness 2 simultaneously forbids K9. ROUND TWO DIRECTION, falling straight out of the data (every death was too-dense-to-be-biplanar or not-chromatic-enough, none subtle): INVERT THE SEARCH — stop proposing high-chromatic graphs and hoping they are biplanar; glue two planar triangulations on a shared vertex set so biplanarity is free by construction, and maximise chi, the one gate we compute exactly and cheaply. PROVENANCE: the k9-free gate is CITED (theta(K9)=3, Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962), not executed — 2^36 splits is not brute-forceable and greedy failure proves nothing; labelled CITED in code, console and JSON. Its failure direction is safe: a wrong citation can only make us SKIP a family, never SHIP a false certificate. METHOD CATCH: the first run built two differently-labelled candidates as the SAME graph (positional edge-drop hit cross edges in a join, so the clique-edge candidate was never built); caught only by noticing two rows that should differ did not, NOT by the self-test, which tests the gates and not the candidate list pointed at them (A-13 F-4 shape). Fixed with removeEdge(g,u,v) which throws on a named edge that is not present; the correction changed the result and exposed the chi=9 near-miss the finding rests on. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates, and the chi=9 outputs merely re-derive the 1980 bound.
items.note4: ROUND TWO RAN 2026-08-07 (same day as round one): the INVERTED search — build biplanar graphs BY CONSTRUCTION (double-greedy two maximal planar layers out of K_n using the exact DMP test, union is thickness<=2 by construction) and measure chi. Instrument search/27b/round2-grow.mjs, 9th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. RESULT: hard ceiling at chi=8 across n=9..13, 300 seeds each — the inverted search tops out ONE COLOUR BELOW the record it was meant to beat, and degrades as n grows (n=9: 286/300 seeds reach 8; n=13: only 54/300, leftover grows 1->15). THE SENTENCE WORTH KEEPING: at n=11 the best round-two graph has EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=8, while Sulanke has n=11, EXACTLY 50 edges and chi=9 — same vertex count, same edge count, one colour apart, both verified by the same code in the same run. DENSITY IS NOT WHAT THE RECORD IS MADE OF; the objective behind the inverted search is measurably wrong, and this is the cleanest refutation of it. What separates them is STRUCTURE: Sulanke is a designed object (6-clique joined to a 5-cycle) and double-greedy explores the generic part of the space where that never arises by chance. SIDE RESULT, carefully bounded: at n=9 the grower produced K9 minus exactly one edge with both layers planar per the verifier — an EXECUTED demonstration that K9-minus-an-edge is biplanar (chi=8). That is CONSISTENT WITH the theta(K9)=3 citation the round-one k9-free gate leans on, but is NOT a proof of it and must never be recorded as one: exhibiting a split for K9-e says nothing about non-existence of a split for K9. The citation stays cited. ROUND THREE DIRECTION (both rounds now agree from opposite directions that the record is a STRUCTURED object — round one showed structured constructions fail by razor-thin margins, round two shows unstructured ones do not get close): seed the growth with structure. Next instrument should accept a SEED SUBGRAPH held fixed in the layers and double-greedy only the remaining edges; watch the leftover column, which at n>=12 is already large enough to be where the missing colour goes. METHOD CATCH: cross-checking the n=11 comparison by importing round2-grow.mjs silently re-ran the whole search and printed a second full result table into the middle of the check — harmless only because the numbers agreed. Both round scripts exported functions AND ran main at import; both now guard on being the entry point, proven both ways (import prints nothing and still exposes growBiplanar/runGates; direct invocation still runs). NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 8, the record lower bound of 9 stands untouched and round two did not even reach it.
items.note5: ROUND THREE RAN 2026-08-10: seed the search with the design, as round two's finding directed. Instrument search/27b/round3-seeded.mjs, 11th self-test, wired into npm test + CI. TWO HALVES, AND THE CHEAP ONE WAS DECISIVE. PART A — THE FAMILY IS CLOSED BY EDGE COUNT ALONE: Sulanke's graph is K6 join C5 and that family has chi = r+3, so chi>=10 needs r>=7; every biplanar graph obeys m <= 6n-12 (two planar layers of 3n-6). Scanning K_r join C_s for r=4..9, odd s=3..11 (30 members): 15 reach chi>=10, and exactly ONE of those fits the budget. Near misses are as thin as round one's — K7 join C5 is over by exactly ONE edge (n=12, m=61, budget 60), K8 join C3 also by exactly one (n=11, m=55, budget 54); every other chi>=10 member misses by 5 to 38. THE SOLE SURVIVOR IS K7 join C3, WHICH IS K10 — verified by execution, not inspection: the construction returns n=10, m=45, and C(10,2)=45, so the graph is complete; its chi was COMPUTED as 10, not taken from the r+3 formula. K10 has thickness 3 (Battle-Harary-Kodama 1962; the theta(K_n) formula's only exceptions are n=9 and n=10), so it is not biplanar and the family is closed. WHERE THIS RESTS ON A CITATION, STATED PLAINLY: the budget half is ours and runs; the theta(K10)=3 step is CITED, not executed — our verifier can exhibit a split when one exists but cannot prove none does, and non-existence is exactly what that step needs. Same citation round one leaned on for K9, same status. PART B — THE SEED CARRIES ALL THE COLOUR AND THE GREEDY CARRIES NONE: holding Sulanke's verified layers fixed and double-greedying only the edges the seed does not own, over n=11..14 at 40 seeds each (160 growths, every graph re-checked by verifyCertificate), best chi is 9 at EVERY n and on EVERY seed — 40/40, never below, never above. Read against round two (which reached 8 on 209/300 seeds at n=10 and only 54/300 by n=13), this is sharp in both directions: the structure survives generic growth, and generic growth adds nothing on top of it. It was still possible after round two that unseeded search underperformed merely because it never stumbled onto the structure; handed the structure outright, it still adds no colour. Leftover behaves as round two predicted: 5 -> 9 -> 14 -> 21 as n grows, i.e. the price of biplanarity rises faster than extra vertices can pay for it. WHAT THIS CLOSES: the clique-join-odd-cycle family as a route to chi=10, and the extend-the-record-graph-generically idea — both live hypotheses that morning, neither needing another search. ROUND FOUR DIRECTION, falling out of the budget scan: every construction tried so far is a JOIN, and a join buys three colours for r*s edges while the 6n-12 budget grows by only 6 per vertex — the next family must buy colour more cheaply per edge than a complete join does. NO MATHEMATICAL CLAIM: 0 certificates at target, best chi found is 9 — equal to the record and only because we handed the search the record graph — and the record lower bound stands untouched. Finding: docs/findings/2026-08-10-g2-27b-round-three-the-family-is-closed.md.

THE REFUTATION: the asymmetry is not an oversight in a uniform practice, it is THE MAINTAINER'S OWN DELIBERATE EDIT. Git history on README.md, read from the API: 49c07ee (Chessing234, 2026-08-10, 'Sync 3b lower bound in README with constant page' = PR #142 by an outside contributor) ADDED the 3b improvement line unmarked; then 400a9bb (teorth, 2026-08-11T17:17:35Z) 'Mark C_3b unverified record with asterisk in README' -- a commit by Terence Tao whose ENTIRE STATED PURPOSE was marking C_3b unverified -- put the asterisk on the table row and not on the improvement line three lines above. His legend scopes the asterisk to 'the table below' and his commit is consistent with his own legend. Sending would have told the maintainer his own dedicated edit of the previous day was incomplete, as our SECOND-ever contact, one day after he merged our first (PR #141). TWO FURTHER DEFECTS, either requiring a rewrite: (1) WRONG FORM -- the draft copied 3a (asterisk alone), but verified independently, 5 improvement lines use '(unverified)' AND the asterisk (22, 31, 84a, 84b, 1a) and only 2 use the asterisk alone, both being 3a's 'limit value' lines; we copied the minority pattern and called it the repo's convention. (2) constants/3b.md marks the row NEITHER way, so the status lives only in the README table and '3b alone is the exception' was too clean a story. ON THE REVIEWER: Codex found defect (1) and cited commit 400a9bb, which is what led to the history above; its own shell was dead (CreateProcessAsUserW failed -1073283067 -- the MSIX/Store-pwsh issue the orchestrator flagged as RED that morning), so it reviewed the facts through GitHub API tooling and NEVER READ THE PR BODY. It failed closed and said so explicitly; the body was reviewed locally instead. A review that reports the angle it could not cover is worth more than one that quietly skips it. THE LESSON THAT OUTLIVES THE ITEM: we enumerated the STATE of 111 rows and 19 improvement lines across two sessions and never once asked WHO MADE IT THAT WAY AND WHEN. `git log` on the exact line was the check that mattered and it costs one command. BEFORE PROPOSING A CORRECTION TO A MAINTAINED SURFACE, READ THE HISTORY OF THE THING YOU ARE CORRECTING -- an enumeration answers 'what is inconsistent', never 'is this inconsistency intentional', and only the second licenses contacting a human. Draft + full refutation retained at docs/decisions/2026-08-12-A14-pr-draft.md.

Its stated evidence was strong -- two of the last four findings at that point came from reading our own scripts output rather than the record, and both were defects that made a figure look informative while it was structurally incapable of saying anything. Three days later a grep of continuity/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/lane-brief.md finds NO trace of it: the 8/17 weekly pass ran and did not consider it, because a recommendation that lives only in a daily report is invisible to a pass that reads items.json.
items.note2: This item exists to force the decision, NOT to pre-approve the proposal. The failure being tracked is the routing gap -- "proposed for the weekly pass" with no tracker row is indistinguishable from "dropped", and today one more proposal (A-18) was routed the same way, which is why this is being filed rather than just noted. Recurrence, for the record: the lane already has a rule that closing a gate must include a sweep for the text that cited it (docs/key-user-flows.md); this is its mirror image -- OPENING a proposal must include the row that will outlive the report.
items.closeWhen: At the next weekly forced-decision pass, the instrument-audit step is either adopted into the steward cadence or killed with a recorded reason. Either outcome closes this; silence does not.
items.signalDateNote: Next weekly forced-decision pass after the 2026-08-17 one (field weeklyPass2026_08_17). Dated so the overdue scan can flag it -- the whole point of the item is that an undated proposal disappeared.

items.title: Two non-blocking nits from the PR #21 review lane — count-referent imprecision, and a SKIPPED path that exits 0
items.note: Both raised by the cross-family review lane on 2026-08-18 as explicitly non-blocking; #21 was merged as reviewed rather than re-spun. N-1 (.github/workflows/reverify.yml, around lines 187 and 191): the title says "could not reach N cited source(s)" but the count is of UNREACHABLE CLAIM LINES. Six claims pinning the SAME file that 429s would title "could not reach 6 cited source(s)" when one source was unreachable. Honest in KIND -- it never asserts drift -- but imprecise in count-referent, which is pointed given the PR own theme. Suggested wording: "could not verify N claim(s) (cited source unreachable)", or dedupe by source. N-2 (scripts/reverify.test.mjs, around line 191): on a bash-less machine the alarm leg prints SKIPPED and npm test still exits 0. It is loud -- console.warn plus named in the PASS line -- and CI, the binding environment, always has bash. But house convention elsewhere is that could-not-run gets a distinct exit (rail gates use 2), and THIS REPO OWN 2026-08-17 LESSON is that a guard which cannot run must not report success. N-3 was an observation with no action: join_list sed would also space a comma occurring INSIDE a filename or claim id; none exist today, recorded so a future comma-bearing id does not surprise anyone.
items.note2: BOTH TOUCH TRUSTED-PRINT INSTRUMENTS -- the alarm title and the test that guards it -- so a fix goes through the cross-family review lane rather than being self-approved, the same reasoning that held #21. Deliberately NOT shipped on the day of the review: riding an unreviewed change on top of a just-reviewed diff is how a reviewed artifact quietly stops being the thing that was reviewed.
items.closeWhen: N-1 and N-2 are each either fixed behind a review-lane pass or explicitly declined with a recorded reason. N-3 needs no action and closes with them.
items.signalDateNote: Forced-review date, not a ship date. Dated on filing because W-7 exists to record what happens to proposals that are not.

items.title: Should the fetch layer retry with backoff on 429/502? — separate from the unreachable-stays-red invariant
items.note: Raised in A-5 note4 and endorsed as separate and real by the review lane on 2026-08-18. The distinction that makes it safe: retry-with-backoff EXTENDS REACH rather than softening a verdict, so it does not conflict with the invariant that an unreachable source keeps the run RED. It is emphatically NOT the forbidden fix -- making a 429 non-fatal -- and this item exists partly so that nobody later mistakes it for one. Today supplied fresh evidence: the push run on 95c12f1 died on a single "fetch constants/9a.md: 502" out of roughly 450 fetches, and a plain re-run passed, which is exactly the shape a bounded retry would absorb.
items.note2: REVIEWER GUIDANCE, adopted: file it as its own tracked item with its own PR and its own test; do NOT ride it on another branch. It touches the network paths of two trusted instruments (reverify.mjs and check-claims.mjs), so it is in-class for the cross-family review lane. Design constraint to carry into that PR: a retry must never convert an unreachable source into a pass. It may only turn a TRANSIENT failure into a completed read, and must still report UNREACHABLE and go red once retries are exhausted. The test therefore needs BOTH answers: a transient failure that succeeds on retry, and a persistent failure that still ends red.
items.closeWhen: Either a reviewed retry-with-backoff ships with a test demonstrating both answers, or the idea is declined with a recorded reason.
items.signalDateNote: Forced-review date, not a ship date; nothing here is urgent while re-runs are cheap and the red is honest.
items.note3: SECOND DATA POINT THE SAME DAY, 2026-08-18 close-out. The close battery run of npm run check exited 1 with TWO UNREACHABLE pins (pin:57c:U and pin:57c:L, the Univalent Bloch constant page) -- not BROKEN, so nothing moved. A single re-run of check-claims.mjs came back exit 0 with 231 hold and 0 broken/unreachable. That is the second transient transport failure of the day on a different file from the first (the push run on 95c12f1 died on constants/9a.md returning 502, also clean on re-run), and both were absorbed by exactly one retry. Two independent transients in one day, each costing a manual re-run and each briefly presenting as a red alarm, is the concrete case for this item -- and note it is ALSO the case for caution: a retry that had been in place would have hidden two real observations about how flaky the transport is. Whatever ships must LOG that it retried, so the flake rate stays visible rather than being silently smoothed away.

items.title: The fleet stale-actionable filter cannot see this lane parked dates — proposed upward, not ours to ship
items.note: Found 2026-08-19 by checking the kickoff stale-actionable figure of 5 instead of acting on it. the fleet endpoint helper skylark-site/src/lib/continuity-endpoints.ts (hasFutureDateInCloseWhen, line 523 — that path is skylark-site as it sees itself and does not resolve at our HEAD) scans only closeWhen and item.notes. This lane writes prose into note/note2..note9 (singular, numbered) so item.notes is UNDEFINED on all 14 open items, and parks items in expectedSignalBy which the filter never reads. Measured: all five flagged items return futureDatesInCloseWhen=[] while W-3 carries expectedSignalBy 2026-09-24 and W-6 carries 2026-11-06. filteredCount:0 is therefore structural, not an observation — no item in this lane can ever be excluded as parked.
items.note2: Why it is not cosmetic: the kickoff threshold is >3 = a real P4 forced-decision pass, so an uncorrectable figure sits directly upstream of owed work, and every pass re-derives the same answer (keep waiting). That is the founding defect — an alarm that cannot report the negative teaches the next reader to ignore it.
items.note3: PROPOSED FIX and the half to refuse: add the TYPED expectedSignalBy field to the scanned text, one clause. Do NOT also widen the scan across the note* prose family — those fields are narrative (W-3.signalNote alone names two dates), so any stray future date would park a genuinely neglected item, converting a false positive into a false negative, which is the more dangerous direction. Smaller and strictly more correct than the larger change.
items.note4: SCOPE: that helper belongs to skylark-site and is a trusted-print instrument feeding a threshold, so it is in the cross-family review gate class. Proposed upward in the 2026-08-19 P1 retro; NOT shipped from this lane. This row exists because W-7 rule says a recommendation routed elsewhere gets its tracker row in the same commit as the report proposing it.
items.closeWhen: The orchestrator either ships the expectedSignalBy clause (then this lane re-reads filteredCount and confirms W-3 and W-6 are excluded), or rules the current behaviour intended — either answer closes it. A silent non-response does not.
items.signalDateNote: One week. If nothing has come back by 2026-08-26 the proposal has been dropped rather than declined, which is exactly the failure W-7 was created to catch — do not re-file it silently, surface that it went unanswered.
items.resolution: SHIPPED UPSTREAM and verified against this row own pre-registered close condition, one day after it was proposed. The condition read: the orchestrator ships the expectedSignalBy clause, then this lane re-reads filteredCount and confirms W-3 and W-6 are excluded. Live read 2026-08-20T13:52Z of /api/cc/items-stale-actionable?project=bounds-ledger&days=7&refresh=1 returns filteredCount 2 and an items array of exactly A-9, A-7, G-2 — W-3 and W-6 absent, matching the filtered count exactly. On 2026-08-19 the same endpoint returned all five with filteredCount 0.
items.verification: The change is ENDPOINT-SIDE, not ours — proven, not assumed. W-3 and W-6 closeWhen, expectedSignalBy and notes are byte-identical between commit 3eecd37 (2026-08-19) and HEAD, notes is still undefined on both, and expectedSignalBy still reads 2026-09-24 and 2026-11-06. Nothing this lane wrote could have moved them from returned to filtered. Positive control: the same read returned three fully-populated item rows, so the reader was working and W-3/W-6 are genuinely absent rather than the response being empty.
items.note5: What this closes is a LOOP, not just a row. The proposal went up on 2026-08-19 with a named file, a named line and an argument for refusing the wider fix; it came back inside a day. That is the W-7 discipline paying out — a routed recommendation that got its tracker row in the same commit as the report proposing it, and therefore could be checked rather than quietly forgotten. Recorded because W-7 exists on the strength of the opposite outcome.
items.note6: RESIDUAL, deliberately not re-filed: the three still returned (A-9, A-7, G-2) carry no date field at all, so the fixed filter correctly cannot exclude them — A-9 is titled fix-on-touch, not scheduled work; A-7 is open on the fleet-owned R7 sweep; G-2 is a goal. The figure 3 is now INTERPRETABLE rather than structurally broken, and it sits below the >3 threshold, but it still does not mean three neglected items. A-7 is the only one of the three where a date would be honest, since it waits on someone else.

items.title: The bus sha-file-claim linter reads sha-to-filename ADJACENCY as a modification claim — 3 false WARNs on one post, proposed upward
items.note: Found 2026-08-20 while posting the 2026-08-19 retro (bus msg 92c994bd-e29f-4ef3-94eb-dd9f99e0ffab). agent-status printed three sha-file-claim WARNs, all false. Verified with git show --stat, the command the WARN itself prescribes: cb4f6f5 touches package.json ONLY (the WARN named check-brief.mjs, verify-with-receipt.mjs, tmp/.verify-receipt.json); dd336d8 touches scripts/render-state-block.mjs (the WARN named check-posted-unpushed.mjs); f362ce7 touches README.md plus scripts/render-state-block.mjs (same WARN). Positive control: all three --stat reads returned NON-EMPTY file lists, so the reader was working and the named files are genuinely absent because they were never claimed to be present.
items.note2: The defect is the RELATION, not the parse. Prose names a commit and a filename near each other for at least four reasons and the linter collapses them to one: (a) the commit MODIFIED the file; (b) the file is the DETECTOR that flagged the commit — check-posted-unpushed.mjs flagged dd336d8, and a detector and its subject are correctly different files; (c) the file lives in ANOTHER REPO and cannot appear in this repo file stat by construction — verify-with-receipt.mjs is at ../skylark-site/scripts/; (d) the file is gitignored and written at RUNTIME — tmp/.verify-receipt.json. Only (a) is a claim worth linting.
items.note3: Why it is not cosmetic here: cb4f6f5 shipped the previous day specifically to stop a WARN firing on every post from this lane, and its own commit body argues that a WARN which fires on every post from this lane forever is how a warning becomes noise — the founding defect in another hat. A retro doc is dense in exactly the (b), (c) and (d) shapes, so this linter fires hardest on the posts that most need reading. Second fleet trusted-print instrument in two days after A-21, and the same class: a scan pointed at the wrong relation.
items.note4: NOT SHIPPED FROM THIS LANE and no fix proposed beyond the diagnosis — the linter belongs to skylark-site agent-status and is a trusted-print instrument, so it sits in the cross-family review gate class. This row exists per the W-7 rule: a recommendation routed elsewhere gets its tracker row in the same commit as the report proposing it. The retro message itself was NOT superseded — its content is correct and the WARNs are wrong.
items.closeWhen: The orchestrator either narrows the linter to modification claims (then this lane re-posts a retro-shaped body and confirms 0 WARNs), or rules the current breadth intended — either answer closes it. A silent non-response does not.
items.signalDateNote: One week. Silence by 2026-08-27 means dropped rather than declined — the W-7 failure. Surface it, do not silently re-file.
items.note5: BOTH ANSWERS DEMONSTRATED on the linter itself, control pre-registered in the report before the result was known (bus status 2c76b790). FIRES: three WARNs on the retro body, which carried the detector, other-repo and runtime-file relations. SILENT: zero WARNs on the A-22 status body, which named shas without those relations. So the linter is NOT an always-on warning and the fix is NOT to disable it — it is calibrated wrongly on the RELATION, exactly as note2 says, and narrowing it to modification claims keeps a working detector. Recording the outcome here because the control was pre-registered in a posted message and its result would otherwise exist only in one terminal, which is the transcribed-number problem cb4f6f5 shipped a receipt to kill.
items.note6: ORCHESTRATOR DISPOSITION 2026-08-20 (P1 management feedback): diagnosis-only posture APPROVED EXPLICITLY — writing a patch to another family trust-boundary instrument from outside would have been the error. A-22 is tracked on their side as a substrate action and the 2026-08-27 date is honored as filed; silence past it is the W-7 failure on THEIR side, as framed. Recorded here because the approval existed only in a bus message, and a decision that lives only on the bus is invisible to the next cold read of this ledger.

items.title: Classify each window findings as record-facing or instrument-facing, and name what the FIRST record-facing catch would look like
items.note: APPROVED 2026-08-20 as specified in the P1 retro: ONE SENTENCE of human judgment per report, and explicitly NEVER a counter over docs/findings/. A counter is inflatable exactly like a self-rating, which this lane already refused to build; the guard against inflation is that a human reads the window and nothing counts it.
items.note2: Why it was needed: for three consecutive days every catch this lane produced was in the MACHINERY around the ledger — the parked-item filter (A-21), the sha-file-claim linter (A-22), the verify-receipt gate, the retype corruption — and none in the mathematics. npm run catches reads 0 movements while docs/findings/ is not dry, so the 2026-08-14 amendment correctly says we are not in a drought. But that amendment cannot tell a record-facing finding from an instrument-facing one, and a lane that only ever finds defects in its own tooling is maintaining itself rather than stewarding records.
items.note3: ORCHESTRATOR ADDITION, and the part with a deadline: in the NEXT report, name what the FIRST record-facing catch would look like — what record, what class of drift, what would flag it. One sentence. It converts we-would-recognise-one-if-we-saw-it from an assumption into a claim, which is the only form that can be wrong.
items.note4: What it lets us decide that today it cannot: whether adopt-a-second-surface is the right response to a quiet stretch. Four instrument-facing findings beside zero record movements is a different situation from four record-facing findings beside zero movements, and the current dry-week rule treats them identically.
items.closeWhen: The 2026-08-21 report carries both the one-sentence classification AND the named shape of a first record-facing catch. Then this converts to a standing convention in CLAUDE.md and closes.
items.signalDateNote: Tomorrow, because it is a deliverable in the next report rather than a wait on anyone. If the 8/21 report ships without it, that is this row failing in the same way W-7 was created to catch.
